correctness.rationale: For each received triple reverse the channel by inserting each symbol in each position and retaining a set of parents. This gives the distinct-source incidence, not a count of positions. My exact check covers all 81 inputs and 27 outputs and confirms the ten symmetry orbits: in units of one eighth, the left sides of (1) are 8 on 51 inputs, 9 on 12, and 10 on 18. The total output and input weights are 75/8 and 21/8. Summing (1) over any valid code counts nonnegative output weights at most twice and nonnegative input corrections at most once, giving size at most floor(171/8)=21. The displayed 21 distinct parents hit each received word exactly twice. Pairwise intersections for the triangle on 0120, 0121, 0210 are {012}, {010,020}, and {021} in pair order (first/second, first/third, second/third). No output hits all three, and the resulting odd cycle cannot lie in a union of two independent sets in the conflict graph. Zero deletions give a unique parent and do not change the maximum.
residual_risks: Exact only for the stated alphabet, block length and deletion/list regime; nondecomposability is established for the displayed optimum, not asserted for every optimum.

value.rationale: A standard fixed-list channel has a meaningful exact finite benchmark here. A checkable rational converse closes the one-codeword gap below twice the unique-list optimum. The attaining code saturates all received words yet cannot be partitioned into two uniquely decodable codes, separating these two ways to use the list allowance at optimum size. The result is not merely a numerical feasible example or an asymptotic-rate claim.
residual_risks: No extrapolation to longer block lengths or larger alphabets.
